extracted.intended_audience: fiction writers and authors considering sensitivity reading / representation of marginalized characters
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and perspective aimed at authors who have written characters from marginalized identities (e.g., transgender characters) and are thinking about authenticity, research, and using sensitivity readers. Focus is on representation in creative writing and on where authors might seek help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing characters outside your identity
rubrics_metrics.description: You have written, let’s say, a transgender character. They might be the protagonist, or their friend, their lover, their sibling… but you are not trans yourself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page frames the common situation where an author who is not part of a community writes a character from that community, implying the need for careful handling and likely sensitivity reading. (Verbatim excerpt used as the page's framing.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Do preliminary research into the community
rubrics_metrics.description: You have done research: you’ve read trans activists; you’ve watched them on YouTube, Instagram, or Twitter; you are slightly aware of trans rights are in your area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page explicitly lists common research steps authors take (reading activists, watching social media, being somewhat aware of local rights). This functions as a baseline criterion or common practice before seeking further feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use community and professional resources (sensitivity readers, editorial community)
rubrics_metrics.description: Salt & Sage Books: We are a creative community of devoted readers, writers, and editors, and we’ve brought together our diverse skills and experiences in a single welcoming place, to help writers like you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site presents itself as a resource/community for authors seeking representation guidance and sensitivity reading; implied criterion is to use community or professional sensitivity readers/editors when representing marginalized identities.
